Featured Press & Research Highlights

Jul 2025 · U of T News

ChronoFlow: an AI model for the ages of stars

Led by PhD student Phil Van-Lane (co-supervised with Gwen Eadie; ApJ, 987, 152), ChronoFlow uses conditional normalizing flows calibrated on open star clusters to infer stellar rotation-age posteriors across the Milky Way, with press coverage in U of T News and Phys.org.

Aug 2024 · AAS Nova

A 5-D map of the Milky Way: AAS Nova featured image

Our lead-author study (Speagle et al. 2024, ApJ, 971, 136) mapping distances, extinctions, and stellar properties for 170 million stars across the Milky Way using brutus was highlighted as an AAS Nova Featured Image.

PressAAS Nova

Jan 2023 · NSF NOIRLab

DECaPS2: a survey of 3.3 billion objects in the Milky Way's plane

The second data release of the Dark Energy Camera Plane Survey (Saydjari et al. 2023, ApJS, 264, 28) catalogued 3.32 billion objects across 6.5% of the night sky in the southern Galactic plane, with press coverage in NSF NOIRLab, Space.com, PBS NewsHour, and Salon.

Results

Oct 2026 · Paper

Tabular foundation models outperform bespoke photometric redshift estimators

Co-authored with postdoctoral fellow Biprateep Dey and accepted for a Spotlight Talk at the NeurIPS 2026 Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS) workshop, our new study shows that pretrained tabular foundation models match or outperform tuned bespoke photo-z estimators with 40x fewer training galaxies and mitigate spectroscopic selection bias via in-context calibration using our open-source lazy-tfm package.

PaperarXiv / NeurIPS ML4PS Spotlight
ADS / Preprint ↗

Sep 2026 · Group

Five new postdoctoral fellows and PhD students join our group at U of T

Postdoctoral fellows Christian Kragh Jespersen (Schmidt AI in Science & CITA National Fellow), Maryum Sayeed (Arts & Science Fellow), and Chloe Cheng (Research Excellence Fellow), along with doctoral students Ian Zhang and Isabelle Huang, join our research group at the University of Toronto.

GroupAstrostatistics Research Team
Current Group →

Sep 2026 · Paper

Model predictive scoring shows specific BAO observations drive the evolving dark energy tension

Led by postdoctoral fellow Tanveer Karim (with Renée Hložek), our new study introduces leave-one-out Bayesian model predictive scoring to isolate which individual observations drive the preference for evolving dark energy, showing that specific DESI BAO redshift bins rather than Type Ia supernovae drive the tension with ΛCDM.

PaperarXiv e-prints

Jul 2026 · Group

Mairead Heiger and Simran Nerval win the 2026 Fieldus Award

Mairead Heiger and Simran Nerval received the department’s Fieldus Award recognizing a high level of research acumen and service. Mairead was honored for her spectroscopic follow-up of the ultra-faint dwarf galaxies Eridanus IV and Centaurus I, her galactic chemical evolution modeling framework, and her leadership as GASA co-chair.

Feb 2026 · Paper

Constraining supernova yields and delay times from dwarf spheroidal galaxies

Led by PhD student Mairead Heiger (with Ting Li and collaborators; ApJ, 1007, 139), our new study uses Bayesian chemical evolution modeling of Milky Way dwarf spheroidal galaxies to constrain Type Ia and core-collapse supernova nucleosynthetic yields and delay-time distributions.

PaperThe Astrophysical Journal

Oct 2025 · Paper

A deep 3-D dust map of the southern Galactic plane from DECaPS2

Co-led with Catherine Zucker and Andrew Saydjari (ApJ, 992, 39), we inferred distances and extinctions for over 550 million stars in the DECaPS2 survey using brutus to construct the deepest 3-D dust map of the southern Milky Way plane.

Nov 2024 · Press

First white dwarf–main-sequence binary candidates in open star clusters

Led by PhD student Steffani Grondin (ApJ, 976, 207), our team combined Gaia DR3, GALEX ultraviolet photometry, and machine learning to identify 52 post-common-envelope white dwarf–main-sequence binary candidates across 38 open star clusters, covered by U of T Arts & Science, Phys.org, and SciTechDaily.

Jan 2022 · Press

The Local Bubble: the Sun sits in a 1,000-light-year void that forms stars

Using 3-D dust maps and Gaia space astrometry, our Nature study (Zucker et al. 2022) showed that virtually all nearby young star-forming complexes lie on the expanding surface of the Local Bubble, covered by CfA, the Harvard Gazette, STScI, and Smithsonian Magazine.
